findings.claim: Lumen Gentium paragraph 7 describes the Eucharist as 'the source and summit of the Christian life' (repeated in the key fact, the exam tip and knowledge check 1).
findings.truth: The phrase is Lumen Gentium 11 ('the fount and apex of the whole Christian life'), quoted at Catechism 1324. Lumen Gentium 7 does not contain it. But the spec itself sets this content 'with reference to Lumen Gentium paragraph 7', so the mark scheme will expect paragraph 7. Option A: leave the lesson as it is, matching the spec citation the student is credited for. Option B: change every mention to Lumen Gentium 11, which is true but no longer matches the spec. Recommendation: Option A, leave it.
findings.evidence: vatican.va Lumen Gentium, paragraphs 7 and 11; spec Area of Study 2A section 2, content 2.2
findings.ruling: Leave: the spec sets paragraph 7 and the mark scheme credits it.

findings.claim: The Catechism of the Catholic Church 2691-2696 recognises pilgrimage as a form of penance and devotion
findings.truth: Catechism 2691 says pilgrimages 'evoke our earthly journey toward heaven and are traditionally very special occasions for renewal in prayer'. It does not present pilgrimage as penance.

summary: Four lessons, 26 findings. The unit teaches the wrong 12-mark command word throughout (Discuss instead of Evaluate) and sets Describe at 3 marks when this spec gives Describe 4 marks; it also repeats invented examiner claims. Doctrinally, lesson 2 wrongly says Orthodox Christians accept purgatory (and a knowledge check marks the true answer wrong), and lesson 4 attributes the phrase 'existential peripheries' to Evangelii Gaudium and pilgrimage-as-penance to Catechism 2691-2696.
